sentences.text: Hulkepholis is an extinct mesoeucrocodylian belonging to the family Goniopholididae that lived in the Escucha Formation in Ariño, Teruel, Spain.
The genus Hulkepholis contains two species: the type species H. willetti and H. plotos.
The species H. plotos is known exclusively from holotype AR-1-2045, which consists of a nearly complete but crushed skull.
Although considered lost by the research community, the holotype of H. willetti was found to be safely accessioned at the Booth Museum in Brighton.
The specific name plotos is derived from the Greek word for 'drifter'.
The holotype of H. willetti was collected by Edgar W. Willett at Cuckfield, West Sussex, from Valanginian-aged strata.
Salisbury and Naish assigned the specimen to the new species Goniopholis willetti in 2011, honoring its collector.
Buscalioni et al. reassigned the species to its own genus in 2013, creating the new combination Hulkepholis willetti.
The genus name Hulkepholis honors John Whitaker Hulke, who originally described the specimen.
The species H. plotos was first described and named by Buscalioni, Alcalá, Espílez, and Mampel in 2013.
H. plotos is known solely from a partial skeleton holotype consisting of a crushed skull, three vertebrae, a rib, a metapodial, and three osteoderms.
The holotype of H. plotos was collected from the early Albian-aged Escucha Formation at Santa Maria Mine in Ariño, Teruel Province, alongside the related species Anteophthalmosuchus escuchae.
Hulkepholis lived from the Valanginian to the Albian stages, approximately 137.05 to 110.1 million years ago.
